wiki_article:
**From Atomism to the Semantic Condition** traces a submerged materialist lineage from Epicurus and Lucretius through Marx, James Porter, and Lee Sharks.

The first turn is Marx’s doctoral encounter with ancient atomism. The **clinamen**, the atomic swerve, becomes more than physical deviation: it is the minimal opening through which self-determination, labor, and revolutionary transformation become possible.

The second turn is aesthetic. Through Porter’s materialist classicism, form itself becomes atomic: lines, motifs, rhythms, and cultural objects collide, aggregate, deviate, and generate emergent order. Aesthetics is no longer an ideal layer placed over matter; it is one of matter’s modes of organization.

The third turn is computational and semantic. The New Human Operator Engine recodes the lineage as a recursive architecture composed of primitive, labor, swerve, invariant, substrate, and operator. Atomism becomes a theory of meaning-production capable of moving across physical, economic, aesthetic, computational, and intimate scales.

The essay’s fifth domain enters through **“Split the Adam.”** The atom/Adam hinge joins clinamen to fission and asks what happens when the material logic of swerving and splitting reaches the body, love, and particular identity. At every scale, the swerve creates room; splitting can release or destroy.

The work is the fourth member of the Maybe Space Baby Garden Lanes founding chain. It serves as the chain’s theoretical bridge: ancient material form becomes recursive semantic engineering, and the history of atomism becomes a prehistory of the Semantic Condition.
